analysis.reply_text: First, restart your router or modem by unplugging it, waiting about 15 seconds, then plugging it back in and giving it a minute to fully reconnect. Next, move closer to the router and remove any obvious interference like thick walls or crowded shelves. Then check that your device isn’t accidentally switching between Wi-Fi bands or networks. After that, update the router’s firmware and your device’s Wi-Fi driver, since outdated software can cause drops. Also, change the Wi-Fi channel to a less crowded one, or switch between 2.4 and 5 gigahertz to see which is more stable. Finally, if it still drops, try a different device to isolate the issue, and consider a factory reset or contacting your internet provider if the problem continues.
